paper_metadata.title: Response to first drug trial predicts outcome in childhood temporal lobe epilepsy

quips_assessment.risk_reasoning: The study provides a clear description of the recruitment period, setting, and inclusion/exclusion criteria. However, it is a retrospective hospital-based cohort rather than a population-based sample, which the authors acknowledge may miss the 'benign end' of the TLE spectrum. While they attempted to capture a mix of severity via satellite centers, the reliance on tertiary/specialty referral patterns introduces a moderate risk of selection bias.

items.label: Source of target population
items.prompt: The source population or population of interest is adequately described for key characteristics (LIST).
items.evidence_snippet: Patients with TLE between 1 and 18 years old seen in the Division of Neurology at Children's Hospital of Philadelphia during 1999 were identified through billing records and chart review.
items.reasoning: The target population (children with TLE in a specific geographic/clinical catchment) is clearly defined.

items.label: Method used to identify population
items.prompt: The sampling frame and recruitment are adequately described, including methods to identify the sample sufficient to limit potential bias (number and type used, e.g., referral patterns in health care)
items.evidence_snippet: Potential patients were identified through centralized billing records, using International Classification of Diseases, Ninth Edition (ICD-9) codes... The study sample consisted of patients referred to and followed by a pediatric neurologist and was not a population-based sample.
items.reasoning: The identification method is clear, but the authors explicitly state it is not population-based, which may exclude patients managed in primary care.

items.label: Recruitment period
items.prompt: Period of recruitment is adequately described
items.evidence_snippet: seen for an outpatient visit in the Division of Neurology at Children's Hospital of Philadelphia (CHOP) during 1999 with onset of epilepsy after 1996.
items.reasoning: The specific year of recruitment and the window for epilepsy onset are provided.

items.label: Place of recruitment
items.prompt: Place of recruitment (setting and geographic location)  are adequately described
items.evidence_snippet: Clinical settings included an urban universitybased outpatient practice and six suburban satellite outpatient practices, which encircle the city of Philadelphia.
items.reasoning: The geographic and clinical settings are well-described.

items.label: Inclusion and exclusion criteria
items.prompt: Inclusion and exclusion criteria are adequately described (e.g., including explicit diagnostic criteria or “zero time” description).
items.evidence_snippet: Eligible subjects for this study had a history of at least two complex partial seizures with clinical seizure semiology suggesting temporal lobe onset... Patients with benign rolandic epilepsy, any other epilepsy syndrome distinct from TLE... were excluded.
items.reasoning: Detailed clinical criteria for inclusion and specific syndromes for exclusion are listed.

items.label: Adequate study participation
items.prompt: There is adequate participation in the study by eligible individuals
items.evidence_snippet: Overall, 1,846 outpatient records with ICD-9 codes 345.4x were reviewed. Of these, 162 patients (8.7%) met inclusion criteria, and 120 patients had at least 2 years of follow-up data.
items.reasoning: While they reviewed all available records, it is unclear how many eligible patients might have been missed due to coding errors or if all identified eligible patients were included (though 120/162 suggests a high inclusion rate of those meeting criteria).

items.label: Baseline characteristics
items.prompt: The baseline study sample (i.e., individuals entering the study) is adequately described for key characteristics (LIST).
items.evidence_snippet: 63 of 120 patients (52.5%) were boys... Mean SD age at epilepsy onset was 6.4 4.1 years in 45 patients with refractory TLE and 7.4 3.9 y in 75 patients who were seizure free.
items.reasoning: Key characteristics like age and sex are provided, stratified by outcome.

quips_assessment.risk_reasoning: The study reports a very high follow-up rate (95% of those eligible and at the 2-year mark). The reasons for exclusion (e.g., suboptimal therapy or early surgery) are transparently reported, and the number of true 'lost to follow-up' cases is minimal (n=6).

items.label: Proportion of baseline sample available for analysis
items.prompt: Response rate (i.e., proportion of study sample completing the study and providing outcome data) is adequate.
items.evidence_snippet: Of these, 162 patients (8.7%) met inclusion criteria, and 120 patients had at least 2 years of follow-up data... 6 were lost to follow-up.
items.reasoning: 120 out of 126 eligible patients (excluding those with <2 years duration) provided data, representing a 95% completion rate.

items.label: Attempts to collect information on participants who dropped out
items.prompt: Attempts to collect information on participants who dropped out of the study are described.
items.evidence_snippet: Not found in text
items.reasoning: The text does not describe specific attempts to re-contact or gather data on the 6 patients lost to follow-up.

items.label: Reasons and potential impact of subjects lost to follow-up
items.prompt: Reasons for loss to follow-up are provided.
items.evidence_snippet: 6 were lost to follow-up, 4 underwent temporal lobectomy before 2 years, and 6 had 'suboptimal AED therapy.'
items.reasoning: Reasons for exclusion from the final analysis are provided, though specific reasons for the 'lost to follow-up' group are not detailed.

items.label: Outcome and prognostic factor information on those lost to follow-up
items.prompt: Participants lost to follow-up are adequately described for key characteristics (LIST).
items.evidence_snippet: Not found in text
items.reasoning: There is no comparison of baseline characteristics between the 120 analyzed and the 6 lost to follow-up.

items.prompt: There are no important differences between key characteristics (LIST) and outcomes in participants who completed the study and those who did not.
items.evidence_snippet: Not found in text
items.reasoning: The sample size of those lost (n=6) is small, but no statistical comparison was provided to confirm lack of difference.

risk_of_bias_assessment.label: Study Attrition Summary
risk_of_bias_assessment.prompt: Loss to follow-up (from baseline sample to study population analyzed) is not associated with key characteristics (i.e., the study data adequately represent the sample) sufficient to limit potential bias to the observed relationship between PF and outcome.

quips_assessment.risk_reasoning: The prognostic factors (especially the primary predictor: failure of first AED) were defined using a clear, standardized algorithm. Data were abstracted independently, and the factors chosen are objective clinical milestones (MRI results, drug failure) that are less susceptible to recall bias in medical records.

items.label: Definition of the PF
items.prompt: A clear definition or description of 'PF' is provided (e.g., including dose, level, duration of exposure, and clear specification of the method of measurement).
items.evidence_snippet: An AED trial was considered a failure if seizures persisted at the maximally tolerated dose. A standard algorithm was used to assess the results of AED trials (figure).
items.reasoning: The primary PF (AED failure) is defined by a specific clinical algorithm.

items.label: Valid and Reliable Measurement of PF
items.prompt: Method of PF measurement is adequately valid and reliable to limit misclassification bias (e.g., may include relevant outside sources of information on measurement properties, also characteristics, such as blind measurement and limited reliance on recall).
items.evidence_snippet: Predictor variables and outcome were abstracted independently... The predictor variables were chosen because they were... reliably measured between observers.
items.reasoning: Independent abstraction and the use of objective clinical records support reliability.

items.prompt: Continuous variables are reported or appropriate cut-points (i.e., not data-dependent) are used.
items.evidence_snippet: The variable 'age at epilepsy onset' was considered as both a continuous variable and a categorical variable with four groups.
items.reasoning: Age was analyzed both ways, and other PFs were naturally categorical.

items.label: Method and Setting of PF Measurement
items.prompt: The method and setting of measurement of PF is the same for all study participants.
items.evidence_snippet: Data were abstracted independently on 5 candidate predictor variables... Clinical seizure semiology and predictor variable data were abstracted from the patient's initial outpatient visit.
items.reasoning: A uniform chart review process was applied to all subjects.

items.label: Proportion of data on PF available for analysis
items.prompt: Adequate proportion of the study sample has complete data for PF variable.
items.evidence_snippet: MRI scans were obtained in 117 of 120 patients (98%).
items.reasoning: Data completeness for the primary predictors was very high.

items.label: Method used for missing data
items.prompt: Appropriate methods of imputation are used for missing 'PF' data.
items.evidence_snippet: Not found in text
items.reasoning: Imputation was not mentioned; however, missing data was minimal (2%).

risk_of_bias_assessment.label: PF Measurement Summary
risk_of_bias_assessment.prompt: PF is adequately measured in study participants to sufficiently limit potential bias.

quips_assessment.risk_reasoning: The outcome (refractory TLE) is clearly defined with a specific timeframe (2 years) and clinical criteria (2 drug failures). While seizure frequency relies on parent/patient reporting, the use of a binary 'seizure-free' vs 'not seizure-free' status is more robust than specific counts.

items.label: Definition of the Outcome
items.prompt: A clear definition of outcome is provided, including duration of follow-up and level and extent of the outcome construct.
items.evidence_snippet: The outcome of interest was 'refractory TLE,' defined as the persistence of any seizures involving impairment of consciousness between 18 and 24 months after epilepsy onset and despite at least 2 maximally tolerated AED trials.
items.reasoning: The outcome is precisely defined by time and clinical status.

items.label: Valid and Reliable Measurement of Outcome
items.prompt: The method of outcome measurement used is adequately valid and reliable to limit misclassification bias (e.g., may include relevant outside sources of information on measurement properties, also characteristics, such as blind measurement and confirmation of outcome with valid and reliable test).
items.evidence_snippet: Predictor variables and outcome were abstracted independently... The binary seizure classification system (seizure free or not seizure free) used in this study is likely more accurate than systems that depend on reporting number of seizures per month.
items.reasoning: Independent abstraction and binary classification reduce measurement error.

items.label: Method and Setting of Outcome Measurement
items.prompt: The method and setting of outcome measurement is the same for all study participants.
items.evidence_snippet: Data were abstracted independently... on seizure frequency outcome at 2 years after epilepsy onset.
items.reasoning: Standardized chart review was used for all participants.

risk_of_bias_assessment.label: Outcome Measurement Summary
risk_of_bias_assessment.prompt: Outcome of interest is adequately measured in study participants to sufficiently limit potential bias.

quips_assessment.risk_reasoning: The study accounts for several clinical confounders (age, MRI findings, risk factors) in a multivariable model. However, as a retrospective study, it cannot account for all potential confounders like socioeconomic status or subtle differences in physician prescribing habits, though they did check for differences in the specific drug used (carbamazepine vs others).

items.label: Important Confounders Measured
items.prompt: All important confounders, including treatments (key variables in conceptual model: LIST), are measured.
items.evidence_snippet: The five predictor variables were age at epilepsy onset, early risk factors for epilepsy, family history of epilepsy in a first-degree relative, temporal lobe abnormality on MRI scan, and outcome of the first AED trial.
items.reasoning: Major clinical factors were measured, but others like IQ or socioeconomic status were not.

items.label: Definition of the confounding factor
items.prompt: Clear definitions of the important confounders measured are provided (e.g., including dose, level, and duration of exposures).
items.evidence_snippet: Early risk factors for epilepsy included a history before 5 years of age of any of the following: febrile seizures, CNS infection... head trauma... or neonatal seizures.
items.reasoning: Confounders like 'early risk factors' were explicitly defined.

items.label: Valid and Reliable Measurement of Confounders
items.prompt: Measurement of all important confounders is adequately valid and reliable (e.g., may include relevant outside sources of information on measurement properties, also characteristics, such as blind measurement and limited reliance on recall).
items.evidence_snippet: The predictor variables were chosen because they were... reliably measured between observers.
items.reasoning: The study prioritized variables with high reliability in retrospective review.

items.label: Method and Setting of Confounding Measurement
items.prompt: The method and setting of confounding measurement are the same for all study participants.
items.evidence_snippet: Clinical seizure semiology and predictor variable data were abstracted from the patient's initial outpatient visit.
items.reasoning: Uniform data collection from initial visits.

items.label: Method used for missing data
items.prompt: Appropriate methods are used if imputation is used for missing confounder data.
items.evidence_snippet: Not found in text
items.reasoning: No imputation was performed.

items.label: Appropriate Accounting for Confounding
items.prompt: Important potential confounders are accounted for in the study design (e.g., matching for key variables, stratification, or initial assembly of comparable groups).
items.evidence_snippet: This retrospective cohort study sought to identify every patient...
items.reasoning: The design was a simple cohort; no matching or stratification was used at the design stage.

items.prompt: Important potential confounders are accounted for in the analysis (i.e., appropriate adjustment).
items.evidence_snippet: A multivariable analysis followed using logistic regression techniques.
items.reasoning: Multivariable regression was used to adjust for the candidate predictors.

risk_of_bias_assessment.label: Study Confounding Summary
risk_of_bias_assessment.prompt: Important potential confounders are appropriately accounted for, limiting potential bias with respect to the relationship between PF and outcome.

quips_assessment.risk_reasoning: The statistical methods are appropriate for the study design. The authors report both bivariate and multivariable results, provide confidence intervals for all estimates, and transparently discuss the predictive values (PPV/NPV) of their model.

items.label: Presentation of analytical strategy
items.prompt: There is sufficient presentation of data to assess the adequacy of the analysis.
items.evidence_snippet: Initially, bivariate analyses were conducted... A multivariable analysis followed using logistic regression techniques.
items.reasoning: The step-by-step analytical approach is clearly described.

items.label: Model development strategy
items.prompt: The strategy for model building (i.e., inclusion of variables in the statistical model) is appropriate and is based on a conceptual framework or model.
items.evidence_snippet: Based on a literature review, 10-17 five candidate predictor variables for refractory TLE were determined before data extraction began.
items.reasoning: Variable selection was based on prior literature, not just statistical significance.

items.prompt: The selected statistical model is adequate for the design of the study.
items.evidence_snippet: Logistic regression indicated that the best model to predict refractory TLE contained only the variable 'failure of first AED trial'
items.reasoning: Logistic regression is appropriate for a binary outcome in a cohort study.

items.label: Reporting of results
items.prompt: There is no selective reporting of results.
items.evidence_snippet: Bivariate analyses of the five predictor variables versus outcome are found in table 1.
items.reasoning: All pre-specified candidate predictors are reported, including those that were non-significant.

risk_of_bias_assessment.label: Statistical Analysis and Presentation Summary
risk_of_bias_assessment.prompt: The statistical analysis is appropriate for the design of the study, limiting potential for presentation of invalid or spurious results.
